raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes the DSpark speculative-decoding output corruption reported in #62417 (and any other model where a prefill-bearing batch can land in a FULL cudagraph).

## Root cause

Under `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, MRV2's varlen decode graphs are captured on a decode-shaped batch (num_reqs x 1 token per request, bucketed by padded token count). At dispatch time, a batch that contains prefill tokens sets `max_query_len=None` (documented as "varlen decode graphs replay decodes only"), but `_is_compatible` treats `desc.max_query_len is None` as "no constraint" — so an unconstrained FULL descriptor matches, and the prefill batch is padded into a decode-shaped graph. The query block layout no longer matches the graph's capture shape, and the target's logits for the prefill's last position come out flattened (observed top-1 logit ~16.9 with the top-5 packed within 0.6, vs the usual 26-31 spike); every subsequently generated token is garbage.

We confirmed this on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 + DSpark k=3: `1 req / 6 tokens` was dispatched into a `num_tokens=8, num_reqs=8, cg=FULL` decode graph. Only 4-token prompts (= bucket size, no padding) looked unaffected, which made the bug look content-dependent.

## Fix

Pass `allow_full=False` through `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` -> `CudaGraphManager.dispatch` whenever the batch has prefill tokens, and skip FULL candidates in that case. Decode-only batches are unaffected.

## Validation (8x RTX PRO 6000, SM120, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, DSpark k=3, fp8 KV)

Applied on both v0.32.0 and the current nightly:

- 7-probe corruption set (short prefill + thinking scaffold, CJK, cat-repeat, chat, tools): byte-identical to the `--enforce-eager` and cudagraph-NONE baselines after the patch; before the patch, 4/7 emitted degenerate loops from the first token.
- chat + tools end-to-end: `17*19=? answer with the number only` -> reasoning + `content=323`; tools request -> structured `tool_calls` (`get_gpu_alert({"node":"gpu-03"})`).
- token-length sweep 1-12 and 6/7/11/12/13/20/110/455: all clean after the patch.
- `--no-swa-bounded-replay` and `engram cpu_offload=false` variants: logits unchanged (rules out replay/engram interactions).

Co-worker evidence, dispatch debug lines, and the probe corpus are archived in xzwgit/llm-test `dsv41-flash-1017-sm120`; the issue thread has the full isolation matrix.

## Notes

A separate, subtler effect remains after this fix and is tracked in #62417: with DSpark on, greedy generation is not token-identical to no-speculation (first token always matches; occasional later-token divergences, e.g. `.` vs `.\n`). Per-row attention bounds (SWA lens, indexer top-k bounds, verify positions) were verified correct by instrumentation; the divergence is k-independent and graph-mode-independent, pointing at multi-row verify numerics rather than dispatch. That is out of scope for this PR.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @xzwgit.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

Rebased onto current main (semantic re-apply after 856b9841 and the new `allow_skip_drafts`/`need_eager` parameters in dp_utils) — mergeable again.

Verified while rebasing that main still has no prefill-vs-FULL-graph guard: `dispatch()` selects candidates purely via `_is_compatible` (token counts / reqs / loras / ubatches), and the pre-existing `max_query_len = None` on prefill batches actually makes them *more* likely to match FULL graphs, since FULL descriptors carry `max_query_len=None` ("does not constrain query length"). The new `decode_graph_eligible`/`prefill_runs_as_decode` state added by the recent spec-decode work feeds input preparation and masks only; it is not consulted during cudagraph candidate selection. So the `allow_full` guard in this PR remains the only thing keeping prefill-bearing batches out of decode-shaped FULL graphs.

Thanks @tomasruizt — agreed, #59986 is the right fix at the right layer. The five DSV4.1 sparse builders declaring `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` is the root cause; once they report `UNIFORM_BATCH` the existing dispatch keeps prefill-bearing batches out of FULL capture on its own, and the model_runner guard in this PR becomes redundant.

One cross-arch data point for the #59986 e2e run: we reproduced the same failure class on SM120 (RTX 6000D / PRO 6000, vLLM 0.32.0 + FlashInfer 0.7.2, DSpark). Same shape as #59970 on a different arch/backend leg — engine boots clean, then the first mixed batch entering a FULL decode-only graph kills the engine; with an allow_full guard, an 87-tier length x concurrency matrix plus agent sessions runs clean. 0.32.0-tree repro + guard snapshot for release users: https://github.com/xzwgit/llm-test/tree/main/sm120-upstream-patches/release-0.32.0-dual-patch (note: SM120 additionally needs the block-size declaration from #60762 — independent axis, both are required to boot and serve there).

Unless there's value in keeping this as a release/0.32 backport, we're glad to close it as superseded once #59986 lands.
Lets close this and support #59986 move forward

Closing in favor of #59986, per the review above and now with both arch legs covered (2xB300 by @tomasruizt, SM120 / RTX PRO 6000D by us — probe table and engine-log confirmation: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59986#issuecomment-6369268785).

For release-0.32.0 users on SM120 who need the fix before #59986 lands: the guard + block-size declaration snapshot for the 0.32.0 tree remains archived at https://github.com/xzwgit/llm-test/tree/main/sm120-upstream-patches/release-0.32.0-dual-patch — #59986's builder changes are an equally valid replacement for the guard half of that snapshot.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

files.patch:
@@ -528,12 +528,15 @@ def dispatch(
         num_active_loras: int,
         max_query_len: int | None = None,
         num_ubatches: int = 1,
+        allow_full: bool = True,
     ) -> BatchExecutionDescriptor:
         """Find matching cudagraph descriptor from priority-ordered candidates."""
         effective_loras = self._resolve_effective_loras(num_active_loras)
         key = (num_tokens, effective_loras)
         if self._graphs_captured and num_tokens > 0 and key in self._candidates:
             for desc in self._candidates[key]:
+                if not allow_full and desc.cg_mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL:
+                    continue
                 if _is_compatible(
                     desc,
                     num_reqs,

@@ -223,6 +223,7 @@ def dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp(
     uniform_decode: bool = False,
     allow_skip_drafts: bool = False,
     dp_sync_state: DPSyncState | None = None,
+    allow_full: bool = True,
 ) -> tuple[BatchExecutionDescriptor, DPSyncState | None]:
     """Pick a cudagraph descriptor for this batch, agreeing it across DP ranks.
 
@@ -287,6 +288,7 @@ def dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp(
             dp_sync_state.uniform_token_count if dp_sync_state else uniform_token_count,
             num_active_loras=num_active_loras,
             max_query_len=max_query_len,
+            allow_full=allow_full,
         )
 
     if dp_size == 1:

@@ -1774,12 +1774,14 @@ def execute_model(
         num_reqs = len(scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens)
         num_toks = scheduler_output.total_num_scheduled_tokens
         max_query_len: int | None = max(scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens.values())
+        allow_full = True
         batch_req_state, uniform_tok_count = self.gather_batch_req_state(
             scheduler_output, dummy_run
         )
         if batch_req_state is not None:
             num_toks = batch_req_state.num_tokens
             if batch_req_state.has_prefill:
+                allow_full = False
                 # Varlen decode graphs replay decodes only, and their bound
                 # alone would admit a short prefill.
                 max_query_len = None
@@ -1818,6 +1820,7 @@ def execute_model(
                 self.ubatch_runner is not None and not skip_attn_for_dummy_run
             ),
             uniform_decode=uniform_tok_count == self.decode_query_len,
+            allow_full=allow_full,
             allow_skip_drafts=scheduler_output.skip_drafts,
         )
